title: Hospitals Struggle as Record Heat Makes Buildings Unsafe
subtitle: Rising temperatures are forcing surgery cancellations and putting patients at risk in aging hospital facilities.

summary.en: Recent heatwaves in England have caused temperatures inside hospital wards to rise to dangerous levels. Many buildings are struggling to stay cool, leading to the cancellation of important surgeries. Cooling systems in operating rooms have failed due to the extreme heat. Staff and patient groups are calling for urgent upgrades to older hospital buildings. There is a growing need to protect vulnerable people as extreme weather becomes more common.
summary.zh: 英格蘭近期的熱浪導致醫院病房內的氣溫升至危險水準。許多建築難以維持涼爽，導致重要手術被迫取消。手術室的冷卻系統因極端高溫而故障。員工與病患團體正呼籲對老舊醫院建築進行緊急升級。隨著極端天氣變得愈發常見，保護弱勢族群的需求也日益迫切。

paragraphs.en: As summer temperatures continue to climb, hospitals across England are facing a difficult challenge. Recent data shows that many medical facilities have become dangerously hot, creating unsafe environments for both patients and healthcare workers. According to The Guardian, some hospitals recorded indoor temperatures as high as 41.8C during the recent heatwaves. This is far above the 28C limit recommended by NHS England to ensure the safety of everyone inside.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著夏季氣溫持續攀升，英格蘭各地的醫院正面臨嚴峻挑戰。最新數據顯示，許多醫療設施的室內溫度已高到危險程度，對病患與醫護人員而言皆不安全。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，在近期的熱浪期間，部分醫院的室內溫度甚至高達攝氏四十一點八度，遠高於英國國家醫療保健服務（NHS England）為確保室內人員安全所建議的攝氏二十八度上限。

paragraphs.en: The problem is causing serious disruptions to medical care. Because of the intense heat, many hospitals have been forced to cancel planned surgeries. This happens when the cooling units in operating theatres—which are often located on the building roof—fail because they cannot handle the extreme weather. When these systems stop working, the rooms become too hot to perform safe procedures. The Guardian reports that some patients are also choosing to cancel their own appointments because the heat makes it too difficult for them to travel to the hospital.
paragraphs.zh: 此問題已嚴重干擾醫療照護。由於酷熱難耐，許多醫院被迫取消預定的手術。當手術室的冷卻系統（通常位於建築物屋頂）因無法負荷極端天氣而故障時，就會發生這種情況。一旦這些系統停止運作，室內溫度便會高到無法進行安全的手術。據《衛報》報導，也有部分病患因天氣太熱、前往醫院的交通過於困難，而選擇自行取消預約。

paragraphs.en: Experts point out that the design of many hospital buildings is part of the problem. Much of the health service’s estate is very old, and these buildings were not built to handle the record-breaking heat seen this summer. David Williams, the deputy director of policy at the NHS Alliance, noted that a long-term lack of investment has left many hospitals with crumbling walls and outdated equipment that is in desperate need of repair. Without modern cooling systems, these buildings simply cannot keep up with the changing climate.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出，許多醫院建築的設計本身就是問題的一部分。醫療服務體系中大部分的資產都相當老舊，這些建築在建造時並未考慮到今年夏天這種破紀錄的高溫。英國國家醫療保健服務聯盟（NHS Alliance）政策副主任大衛·威廉斯（David Williams）指出，長期缺乏投資導致許多醫院牆面剝落、設備過時，急需修繕。若沒有現代化的冷卻系統，這些建築根本無法應對氣候變遷。

paragraphs.en: The impact of the heat is being felt across the entire healthcare system. Ambulance services are finding it difficult to keep certain medications at the correct temperature inside their vehicles. To help staff stay safe, some ambulance trusts have even changed their dress codes, allowing crews to wear shorts instead of long trousers. Meanwhile, many hospitals and local doctor offices are trying to help by scheduling appointments for elderly or frail patients only during the early morning or late evening, when the air is cooler.
paragraphs.zh: 高溫的影響已波及整個醫療體系。救護車服務單位發現，要在車內將特定藥物維持在正確溫度變得十分困難。為了協助工作人員保持安全，一些救護車信託機構甚至修改了服裝規定，允許救護人員穿著短褲而非長褲執勤。同時，許多醫院與基層診所也試圖透過調整門診時間來提供協助，將年長或體弱病患的預約安排在氣溫較涼爽的清晨或傍晚。

paragraphs.en: In response to these findings, the Liberal Democrats have called for urgent action from government ministers. They suggest creating a new “NHS rapid adaptation unit.” The goal of this group would be to “heatproof” hospitals and care homes. This would involve installing better air conditioning and upgrading buildings so they can withstand future heatwaves. Helen Morgan, a health spokesperson for the party, stated that hospitals are becoming “dangerously hostile environments” and that the government must act now to make these facilities fit for the future.
paragraphs.zh: 針對這些調查結果，自由民主黨（Liberal Democrats）已呼籲政府官員採取緊急行動。他們建議成立一個新的「醫療服務快速適應小組」，目標是為醫院與護理之家進行「防熱工程」。這將涉及安裝更好的空調設備並升級建築，使其能抵禦未來的熱浪。該黨衛生發言人海倫·摩根（Helen Morgan）表示，醫院正逐漸變成「危險且惡劣的環境」，政府必須立即採取行動，讓這些設施能適應未來需求。

paragraphs.en: Some hospitals are already trying to manage the situation on their own. Many have started renting temporary air conditioning units to keep wards cool. One trust alone has rented at least 600 of these units to help manage the temperature. However, staff organizations warn that this is only a temporary fix. There is growing concern that nurses and other medical staff are becoming exhausted or even fainting while trying to work in these high-temperature conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 部分醫院已開始自行設法應對。許多醫院已著手租用臨時空調設備來維持病房涼爽。單單一個信託機構就至少租用了六百台這類設備來控制溫度。然而，員工組織警告這只是權宜之計。各界日益擔憂護理師與其他醫護人員在這種高溫環境下工作，正變得精疲力竭，甚至出現昏倒的情況。

paragraphs.en: The situation highlights a broader issue regarding how public buildings are prepared for a changing climate. As heatwaves become more frequent and intense, the ability of hospitals to provide consistent care is being tested. The data collected by the Liberal Democrats and the NHS Alliance serves as a warning that without significant investment, the health service will continue to struggle. For now, hospitals remain in a difficult position, trying to balance the need for urgent medical procedures with the reality of buildings that are struggling to stay cool.
paragraphs.zh: 此情況凸顯出一個更廣泛的議題，即公共建築應如何為氣候變遷做好準備。隨著熱浪變得愈發頻繁且劇烈，醫院提供穩定照護的能力正受到考驗。自由民主黨與醫療服務聯盟所收集的數據是一項警訊，若無重大投資，醫療服務體系將持續陷入困境。目前，醫院仍處於兩難處境，必須在進行緊急醫療處置的需求，與建築難以維持涼爽的現實之間取得平衡。

keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「房地產」或「遺產」，這裡指醫院體系的建築群。文中：Much of the health service’s estate is very old, and these buildings were not built to handle the record-breaking heat seen this summer.

quiz.question: What is the primary cause of the cancellation of planned surgeries in hospitals during heatwaves?

options.A: Patients are unable to travel to the hospital due to the heat.
options.B: Cooling systems in operating rooms located on roofs fail to function.
options.C: Staff members are exhausted and fainting, leading to labor shortages.
options.D: The NHS recommends canceling all non-emergency procedures above 28C.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，手術取消是因為位於建築屋頂的冷卻設備無法應對極端天氣而失效，導致手術室溫度過高。選項 A 雖然在文中提到，但這是病人自行取消預約的原因，而非醫院取消手術的原因。選項 C 是第六段提到的勞工問題，並非手術取消的主要技術原因。選項 D 錯誤，因為 28C 是 NHS 的安全建議標準，而非強制取消所有手術的規定。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might simply renting temporary air conditioning units be considered an inadequate long-term solution?

options.A: The units are too expensive for the Liberal Democrats to fund.
options.B: The units are only effective for cooling small doctor offices, not large hospitals.
options.C: The underlying problem is the structural decay and poor design of aging hospital buildings.
options.D: Nurses and medical staff have refused to work with temporary cooling equipment.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。透過第三段與第六段的連結可知，醫院面臨的是建築結構老舊、牆壁破損與設備過時的根本問題。租用臨時冷氣只是治標不治本，無法解決建築物本身無法適應氣候變遷的結構性缺陷。選項 A 文中未提及經費來源與該政黨的關係。選項 B 文中並未指出該設備對大型醫院無效。選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到員工因高溫感到疲憊或昏倒，並未提到拒絕使用臨時設備。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'hostile' mean as used in the phrase 'dangerously hostile environments'?

options.B: Extremely difficult and harmful to be in.
options.C: Intentionally designed to exclude certain groups.
options.D: Likely to cause a physical conflict or fight.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「hostile」形容的是環境對人體健康具有威脅性且極度不舒適，而非指環境具有敵意或會主動攻擊人。選項 A 將其誤解為社交上的不友善。選項 C 與 D 雖然在其他語境下可能與「hostile」有關，但在這篇文章討論醫院因高溫而導致環境惡化的脈絡中，這兩個選項並不符合該詞在描述極端氣候對建築影響時的本意。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: The Liberal Democrats are the only group actively seeking to solve the hospital heat crisis.
options.B: Ambulance services are the most affected part of the healthcare system during heatwaves.
options.C: Hospitals need to change their dress codes to help staff cope with rising temperatures.
options.D: Aging hospital infrastructure is ill-equipped for climate change, necessitating urgent investment and modernization.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章從頭到尾都在討論醫院因建築老舊、無法應對氣候變遷導致的高溫，進而影響醫療服務與病人安全，並強調需要政府介入投資與現代化改造。選項 A 僅是文章的一部分，非核心主旨。選項 B 與 C 僅是文章中提到的特定細節或應變措施，並非全文探討的廣泛問題。因此 D 最能概括全文的主旨。
